quote:
For lagoon creation to be proﬁtable for a landholder, payments
would likely need to ensure farmers achieve a beneﬁt to cost
ratio of at least 1:1 over the evaluation period (15 years in this
study). To achieve a beneﬁt to cost ratio of 1:1 over 15 years
without the subsidy for lagoon construction and without
including beneﬁts from reduced inundation, but still accounting
for the improved productivity on land elevated with excavated
spoil, payments would need to be $8076/ha of wetland (in
2019 AUD$) when elevated land can be converted from cattle
fattening to four-ratoon cane rotation, or $10,684/ha of wetland
(in 2019 AUD$) when elevated land is converted from two-
ratoon to four-ratoon cane rotation.

relationship.condition: Project payments support financial viability of rural freshwater lagoon creation where private productivity benefits do not cover construction and maintenance costs.
relationship.note: Case-specific financial model; no universal funding threshold, credit-access effect, or suitability score.

context.practice_as_described: Excavated freshwater drainage lagoons and arterial drains integrated into sugarcane farms; excavation spoil raises neighbouring fields. Baseline: frequently flooded land supporting cattle fattening or sugarcane with plant cane plus two ratoon harvests. Improved land supports plant cane plus four ratoon harvests. A ratoon is regrowth harvested after initial planting.
context.note: Financial viability is modelled, not a causal estimate of adoption. justification_quote:
The cost incurred by the landholder comprises 33% of
the construction cost of their on-farm drainage lagoon (the
remaining 67% of construction costs being covered by the
scheme subsidy), plus any on-going maintenance costs.
